column1: The positive and negative effects of the chemical known as the ‘love hormone’
column2: 这种被称为“爱情激素”的化学物质，既有积极影响，也有消极影响。
column3: positive and negative effects|积极和消极的影响

column1: Oxytocin is a chemical, a hormone produced in the pituitary gland in the brain.
column2: 催产素是一种化学物质，是脑内垂体产生的一种激素。

column1: It was through various studies focusing on animals that scientists first became aware of the influence of oxytocin.
column2: 科学家最初是通过多项动物研究认识到催产素具有何种影响的。

column1: They discovered that it helps reinforce the bonds between prairie voles, which mate for life, and triggers the motherly behaviour that sheep show towards their newborn lambs.
column2: 他们发现，草原田鼠终生结伴，催产素有助于加强配偶间的联结。这种激素也能触发母羊照料初生羊羔的行为。

column1: It is also released by women in childbirth, strengthening the attachment between mother and baby.
column2: 女性在分娩时也会释放这种激素，加强母亲和婴儿之间的依恋。

column1: Few chemicals have as positive a reputation as oxytocin, which is sometimes referred to as the ‘love hormone’.
column2: 催产素有时被称为“爱情激素”，少有化学物质拥有像它这样正面的声誉。
column4: positive a reputation|如此正面的声誉

column1: One sniff of it can, it is claimed, make a person more trusting, empathetic, generous and cooperative.
column2: 据称，只要嗅吸一下这种激素，就能使人更信任他人、更能共情、更慷慨，也更乐于合作。

column1: It is time, however, to revise this wholly optimistic view.
column2: 然而，这种全然乐观的看法，该修正了。
column3: It is time|到了该……的时候

column1: A new wave of studies has shown that its effects vary greatly depending on the person and the circumstances, and it can impact on our social interactions for worse as well as for better.
column2: 新一轮研究表明，催产素的作用因人、因情境而大不相同。它对我们的社交互动既可能有益，也可能带来负面影响。
column3: new wave of studies|新一轮研究
column8: for worse as well as for better|既可能带来坏处，也可能有益

column1: Oxytocin’s role in human behaviour first emerged in 2005.
column2: 2005年，催产素在人类行为中的作用首次显现出来。

column1: In a groundbreaking experiment, Markus Heinrichs and his colleagues at the University of Freiburg, Germany, asked volunteers to do an activity in which they could invest money with an anonymous person who was not guaranteed to be honest.
column2: 在一项开创性实验中，德国弗赖堡大学的马库斯·海因里希斯和同事让志愿者参加一项活动，他们可以把钱交给一个匿名的人投资，但对方未必诚实。

column1: The team found that participants who had sniffed oxytocin via a nasal spray beforehand invested more money than those who received a placebo instead.
column2: 研究团队发现，与事先接受安慰剂的参与者相比，通过鼻喷剂吸入催产素的参与者投入了更多的钱。

column1: The study was the start of research into the effects of oxytocin on human interactions.
column2: 这项实验开启了对催产素如何影响人际互动的研究。

column1: ‘For eight years, it was quite a lonesome field,’ Heinrichs recalls.
column2: “有整整八年，这还是个相当冷清的研究领域。”海因里希斯回忆说。
column4: lonesome field|鲜有人涉足的领域

column1: ‘Now, everyone is interested.’
column2: “现在大家都有兴趣了。”

column1: These follow-up studies have shown that after a sniff of the hormone, people become more charitable, better at reading emotions on others’ faces and at communicating constructively in arguments.
column2: 这些后续研究表明，人们嗅吸催产素后更乐善好施，更善于从面部表情辨别他人的情绪，也更能在争论中开展建设性沟通。

column1: Together, the results fuelled the view that oxytocin universally enhanced the positive aspects of our social nature.
column2: 这些结果合在一起，使人们更加相信，催产素能普遍强化人类社会天性中积极的一面。

column1: Then, after a few years, contrasting findings began to emerge.
column2: 然而，几年后，相反的研究结果开始出现。
column3: after a few years|几年之后
column4: contrasting findings|截然不同的研究结果

column1: Simone Shamay-Tsoory at the University of Haifa, Israel, found that when volunteers played a competitive game, those who inhaled the hormone showed more pleasure when they beat other players, and felt more envy when others won.
column2: 以色列海法大学的西蒙娜·沙迈-措里发现，志愿者参加竞争性游戏时，吸入过催产素的志愿者在击败对手后表现出更大的快感，别人胜出时又更为嫉妒。

column1: What’s more, administering oxytocin also has sharply contrasting outcomes depending on a person’s disposition.
column2: 此外，一个人的性情不同，给予催产素也会产生截然不同的结果。

column1: Jennifer Bartz from Mount Sinai School of Medicine, New York, found that it improves people’s ability to read emotions, but only if they are not very socially adept to begin with.
column2: 纽约西奈山医学院的珍妮弗·巴茨发现，催产素能增强人们识别情绪的能力，但这种作用只见于原本就不太擅长社交的人。
column4: ability to read emotions|识别情绪的能力

column1: Her research also shows that oxytocin in fact reduces cooperation in subjects who are particularly anxious or sensitive to rejection.
column2: 她还发现，对于特别焦虑或对遭到拒绝特别敏感的受试者，催产素实际上会降低他们合作的意愿。

column1: Another discovery is that oxytocin’s effects vary depending on who we are interacting with.
column2: 另一项发现是，催产素的作用还取决于我们在和什么人打交道。

column1: Studies conducted by Carolyn DeClerck of the University of Antwerp, Belgium, revealed that people who had received a dose of oxytocin actually became less cooperative when dealing with complete strangers.
column2: 比利时安特卫普大学的卡罗琳·德克勒克开展的研究表明，受试者接受一定剂量的催产素后，与完全陌生的人打交道时实际上更不愿合作。

column1: Meanwhile, Carsten De Dreu at the University of Amsterdam in the Netherlands discovered that volunteers given oxytocin showed favouritism: Dutch men became quicker to associate positive words with Dutch names than with foreign ones, for example.
column2: 另一方面，荷兰阿姆斯特丹大学的卡斯滕·德德勒发现，接受催产素的志愿者表现出偏爱自己群体的倾向：例如，荷兰男性将褒义词与荷兰人名联系起来的速度，比与外国人名联系起来更快。

column1: According to De Dreu, oxytocin drives people to care for those in their social circles and defend them from outside dangers.
column2: 德德勒认为，催产素会促使人们关心自己社交圈里的人，并保护他们免受外部威胁。

column1: So, it appears that oxytocin strengthens biases, rather than promoting general goodwill, as was previously thought.
column2: 因此，催产素似乎会强化偏向，而不像先前认为的那样，普遍增进对人的善意。

column1: There were signs of these subtleties from the start.
column2: 其实，这些微妙之处从一开始就有迹可循。

column1: Bartz has recently shown that in almost half of the existing research results, oxytocin influenced only certain individuals or in certain circumstances.
column2: 巴茨最近指出，在已有研究结果中，近一半显示催产素只对特定的人，或只在特定情境下，才会产生影响。
column4: existing research results|已有的研究结果

column1: Where once researchers took no notice of such findings, now a more nuanced understanding of oxytocin’s effects is propelling investigations down new lines.
column2: 研究人员过去并不关注这类发现，如今，对催产素作用有了更细致的认识，正在推动研究沿新的方向展开。
column4: took no notice of|对……不予理会
column5: nuanced understanding|细致而有层次的认识

column1: To Bartz, the key to understanding what the hormone does lies in pinpointing its core function rather than in cataloguing its seemingly endless effects.
column2: 在巴茨看来，要理解催产素的作用，关键是找准它的核心功能，而不是把它看似数不清的效应一一罗列。

column1: There are several hypotheses which are not mutually exclusive.
column2: 对此有几种假说，彼此并不排斥。
column4: not mutually exclusive|彼此并不排斥

column1: Oxytocin could help to reduce anxiety and fear.
column2: 催产素可能有助于减轻焦虑和恐惧。

column1: Or it could simply motivate people to seek out social connections.
column2: 也有可能，它只是促使人们主动寻求人际联系。

column1: She believes that oxytocin acts as a chemical spotlight that shines on social clues — a shift in posture, a flicker of the eyes, a dip in the voice — making people more attuned to their social environment.
column2: 她认为，催产素就像化学聚光灯，会照亮一些社交信号，如姿势微变、目光一闪或声音放低，使人更能觉察周围的社交环境。
column6: flicker of the eyes|目光的短暂变化
column7: dip in the voice|声音放低

column1: This would explain why it makes us more likely to look others in the eye and improves our ability to identify emotions.
column2: 这也就能解释，为什么催产素使我们更愿意直视他人的眼睛，也增强了辨别情绪的能力。
column5: look others in the eye|直视他人的眼睛

column1: But it could also make things worse for people who are overly sensitive or prone to interpreting social cues in the worst light.
column2: 但对于过度敏感或容易对社交信号作最坏解读的人，它也可能使情况恶化。
column8: in the worst light|从最糟糕的角度

column1: Perhaps we should not be surprised that the oxytocin story has become more perplexing.
column2: 也许，催产素的作用越研究越令人困惑，我们不必对此感到意外。
column5: story|n. 围绕它的研究情况

column1: The hormone is found in everything from octopuses to sheep, and its evolutionary roots stretch back half a billion years.
column2: 从章鱼到绵羊，各种动物体内都有这种激素，它的进化渊源能追溯到5亿年前。

column1: ‘It’s a very simple and ancient molecule that has been co-opted for many different functions,’ says Sue Carter at the University of Illinois, Chicago, USA.
column2: 美国伊利诺伊大学芝加哥分校的苏·卡特说：“这是一种非常简单而古老的分子，在进化中被借用于许多不同的功能。

column1: ‘It affects primitive parts of the brain like the amygdala, so it’s going to have many effects on just about everything.’
column2: 它影响着大脑中一些古老的部位，比如杏仁核，因此几乎方方面面都会受到它的多重影响。”
column4: primitive parts|进化上较古老的部位
column7: just about everything|几乎所有事物

column1: Bartz agrees.
column2: 巴茨赞同这种看法。

column1: ‘Oxytocin probably does some very basic things, but once you add our higher-order thinking and social situations, these basic processes could manifest in different ways depending on individual differences and context.’
column2: “催产素的作用本身可能十分基础，但把人类的高级思维和社交情境考虑进来，这些基础过程就可能因为个体差异和具体背景，以不同的方式表现出来。”
